team_project.team_project_title: Recreating the Homepage: A UI Imitation Study in Figma
team_project.team_project_description: One of the best ways to improve UI design skills is by studying and recreating existing interfaces. Rebuilding a homepage in Figma helps you understand important design decisions such as spacing, navigation structure, call-to-action placement, and visual hierarchy.

User Interface imitation helps users observe design details, but effective HCI practice also requires evaluation and improvement. In this activity, you will analyze Facebook’s mobile homepage and identify usability issues based on HCI principles, such as cognitive overload, poor system status visibility, overcrowded navigation, inconsistent icons, and accessibility concerns like contrast, font size, and touch targets.

team_project.team_project_title: Google’s Material 3 Design Mobile App Prototype
team_project.team_project_description: Modern mobile applications require not only functionality but also consistent and user-centered design. Google’s Material 3 provides a comprehensive design system that helps developers and designers create visually appealing, accessible, and cohesive user interfaces.

Mobile applications often require users to register and log in to access personalized features. In Mobile HCI, effective authentication design helps users complete these tasks easily on small screens. Multi-step registration forms improve usability by dividing information into smaller sections and reducing cognitive load.

team_project.team_project_title: Responsive and Adaptive Design: Mobile and Web Application Prototype
team_project.team_project_description: Modern applications are used across multiple devices, making adaptable interfaces essential. Responsive design adjusts layouts based on screen size, while adaptive design uses specific layouts for different devices. Both improve usability, accessibility, and user experience.
